items.claim: Big Mac Index originated as a light-hearted purchasing-power comparison and is useful as a PPP illustration, not a complete currency model.
items.primary_source_target: The Economist Big Mac Index methodology/data
items.risk_if_wrong: Opening chapter misstates the foundational example.

items.claim: Work-time comparisons make prices more human but depend on wage assumptions and local method.
items.primary_source_target: UBS Prices and Earnings; original iPhone work-time methodology

items.claim: Lipstick Index is a media-friendly recession hypothesis with contested empirical support.
items.preferred_source_type: high-quality journalism plus underlying market/economic evidence
items.primary_source_target: Leonard Lauder attribution and later empirical critiques

items.claim: Men's Underwear Index is attributed to Greenspan and remains weakly evidenced as a formal macro signal.
items.preferred_source_type: primary attribution or reputable economics journalism
items.primary_source_target: Greenspan attribution and apparel-sales evidence
items.risk_if_wrong: Highly memorable title object becomes unreliable.

items.claim: Skyscraper Index is better treated as myth/correlation story than predictive law.
items.primary_source_target: Skyscraper Index original formulation and later tests

items.claim: Cigarette-equivalent pollution is a risk analogy, not a literal chemical equivalence to smoking.
items.preferred_source_type: methodology source plus health institution guidance
items.primary_source_target: Berkeley Earth cigarette-equivalence method; WHO PM2.5 guidance

items.claim: PM2.5 concentration, AQI, annual exposure and short-term spikes are not interchangeable.
items.primary_source_target: WHO and OpenAQ definitions

items.claim: A measure can lose integrity when people optimize directly for it.
items.preferred_source_type: academic / original formulation plus applied case
items.primary_source_target: Goodhart's law references and a concrete governance case

items.claim: LIBOR manipulation is a clear example of a trusted benchmark becoming a governance/manipulation case.
items.primary_source_target: US DOJ / regulator LIBOR manipulation records

items.claim: AI benchmarks function as an index family and inherit interpretive/incentive problems.
items.primary_source_target: Stanford AI Index, SWE-Bench and benchmark methodology pages

items.claim: Latte comparisons can support the everyday-price family but should not be over-weighted.
items.preferred_source_type: reputable secondary plus underlying data where used
items.primary_source_target: Starbucks/latte index source used in final prose
items.risk_if_wrong: Support example becomes stale or thin.

items.claim: Baltic Dry Index reflects dry bulk shipping market information and is more grounded than consumer folklore.
items.primary_source_target: Baltic Exchange methodology and current explanation

items.claim: Container freight measures capture different trade dynamics than dry bulk shipping.
items.primary_source_target: Freightos Baltic Index methodology
items.risk_if_wrong: Freight examples collapse into one undifferentiated shipping story.

items.claim: Electricity demand can act as a physical-economy signal in context.
items.primary_source_target: Ember or Electricity Maps methodology

items.claim: Date Night and urban lifestyle comparisons can support affordability but are context-sensitive.
items.primary_source_target: Numbeo or chosen cost-of-living data methodology

items.claim: Doing Business is a governance example for measurement incentives and discontinuation.
items.primary_source_target: World Bank Doing Business discontinuation/review documents

items.claim: Government AI readiness rankings are index-like but should be used cautiously.
items.primary_source_target: Oxford Insights Government AI Readiness Index methodology

items.claim: CO2 flight equivalents are useful translation devices but require clear assumptions.
items.primary_source_target: Our World in Data / Global Carbon Project methodology

items.claim: Hemline Index belongs as optional folklore, not as a core economic proof.
items.primary_source_target: Only needed if included in manuscript V1
items.risk_if_wrong: Low if excluded or clearly marked folklore.

items.claim: IKEA Billy Index can support the purchasable-object family if concise.
items.primary_source_target: Original Billy Index source

items.claim: Restaurant reservations may be used as a nowcasting support example.
items.primary_source_target: Specific reservation-data source chosen during drafting
items.risk_if_wrong: Optional support example can be removed.

items.claim: Owner project experience may appear only as method context, not promotion.
items.primary_source_target: ABVX evidence only if editorially useful
